All that extra money will end up floating back to the top into people's pockets who don't need it. What'll end up happening is landlords will start thinking to themselves "well, I know that Cracker Joe is making at least $15 and hour now, so he should be able to afford way more for the shitty apartment he wants to rent out from me". Other industries will do the same until next thing you know Cracker Joe's $15 and hour raise puts him exactly where he was to begin with: broke and nickel and dimed to death.

Wages are low because of outsourcing for cheaper alternatives. And guess what? California's law only encourages that more. If you have factory workers making minimum wage, and you have to increase their wage that much if you stay in California, but you can keep it low if you move somewhere else, those jobs will move somewhere else. And as a result, unemployment goes up, businesses leave, tax revenue goes down, etc. It's extremely similar to what's happening in Chicago and Illinois, only Chicago and Illinois are driving business away with taxes and regulations (Chicago tried to tax Netflix just a little bit ago, they're out of control).

People do need a living wage, and people aren't paid enough. But forcing wages to a certain standard won't increase the quality of living. It'll increase the amount of jobs that move to other states, or worse, to places like China or southern Asia.

But, as this article mentioned, the people who will feel this the worst are the small business owners. Compare a small family owned diner to a fast food place. The fast food place is owned by a giant corporation with millions of dollars in profits, they can afford the wage, they just don't want to pay it. Meanwhile, that family diner that barely scrapes by? They go out of business because they can't afford to pay the minimum wage, as they don't have the revenue or profit to pay for it. You'll be seeing that a lot in California, specially when you couple it with the fact that the larger companies can afford to move out of state and the smaller ones can't. You'll start seeing a lot of family owned business go out of business and replaced by things like Wal-Mart, McDonalds, etc with this new state-wide minimum wage.

Not to mention, if this minimum wage is really state-wide, why would you live in a city with a higher cost of living, when you can move to a small town and make the same amount of money and enjoy a lower cost of living? You'll probably see a huge migration away from urban areas and into more affordable places to live, provided people won't move out of California in the first place.
